summary: A Cherokee National Forest lookout in Cocke County, Tennessee; its live-in block cab became an open steel viewing deck around 2013, and the registers disagree on its status.

facts.design: Two-story cinderblock lookout cab; cab later removed and replaced by an open all-steel viewing platform
facts.status_note: The live-in cab was removed and replaced by an open steel viewing deck, dated 2013 by one source.

access.note: Opened to the public after the 2013 conversion per the Eastern US lookouts site; a user-submitted travel listing says the Forest Service opened it to visitors. No official notice was found.

visit.trail_note: Gravel parking lot, then a short walk up the hill to the tower, per a travel listing

events.note: A platform mounted between three chestnut trees stood on the site
Visit by Jeff Flanary on September 20, 2008: decent shape; needs paint, glass, door and interior restoration; not staffed
Converted to an all-steel viewing platform for public use after vandalism to the original structure; about $23,000 spent; the live-in cabin was removed
Registered January 3, 2015 as US 1087, TN 23; nominated by Jeff Flanary
Registered March 16, 2015 as US 1589, TN 2, on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register

notes_for_editor: No source read gives a build year for the block tower. Search snippets (Pinterest, Tripadvisor) say 1950s and 'since 1926' but were not fetched and are not cited. The 2013 conversion date rests on one source (Eastern US lookouts). The 2017 blog does not give a year. Access 'public' rests on a user-submitted travel listing and the Eastern US lookouts site's 'for public use'; the 2008 visit sheet shows no signs. Please confirm current access with the Cherokee National Forest before publishing. The NHLR's description still reads as a block tower and may be out of date. The tnlandforms GPX (cached) lists the site as 'Cocke cnf standing'; it is not cited because the GPX is not a readable page. The record's material 'masonry' comes from the NHLR and may be out of date after the 2013 conversion; no correction was proposed for material.
